edit.description: `writeTickVerdict`'s window slice, the one place a verdict leaves the retained set, and `MAX_TICK_VERDICTS`'s doc which states what the bound covers
the run-window edge (`startedAfter`, the `fsStamp` string compare), shared with the trim rather than respelled beside it
the verdict-history retention cases, beside the window's own
the in-flight count's cases, the seam the live-run clause exists to keep right

summary: Nothing trims .flume/rendered-prompts/, which spec/prompt.md now bounds by the verdict history's own retention, and flume status readdirs it on every call

per.section: The rendered prompt is persisted before the agent runs

acceptance: a rendered prompt is removed once no retained verdict names it as `promptPath` and it is outside a live run's window, so the directory is bounded by the verdict history's own retention and by no second setting. The retained set is read off the history's *lines*, the alphabet `MAX_TICK_VERDICTS` bounds — a line `isTickVerdict` declines still names its prompts and still holds them. The live-run window is the one edge `src/runSpend.ts` already compares against, shared not respelled, so the in-flight count over a trimmed directory stays exactly today's. A trim failure never fails the tick whose verdict it follows.
tests: a rendered prompt no retained verdict names is removed when the history window drops the verdict that named it
a rendered prompt inside a live run's window is kept though no verdict names it yet
notes: Ruled in the inbox this tick; f4f77bb1 replaced `Retention is the operator's`. Verified: `recordRenderedPrompt` (`src/tickAttempt.ts:874`) only ever writes, `src/tickVerdict.ts:1171` is the window slice, and nothing else deletes from the dir. `readRunSpend` (`src/runSpend.ts:83`) readdirs the whole directory per `flume status` call. No live supervisor means no window, and the tip claim bounds a bare tick to one per ref.
